title: Real-Time Chat Application
intro: Design a highly scalable 1-on-1 and group chat system supporting 50M+ concurrent persistent connections, message delivery receipts, and presence tracking.
objectives: Establish stateful WebSocket connection clusters with Redis Pub/Sub backbones.
Design wide-column message storage (Cassandra/ScyllaDB) partitioned by conversation ID.
Implement real-time online/offline presence tracking clusters.
body:
### Connection Tier & Message Routing
- **Persistent Connections**: Mobile and web clients maintain bi-directional WebSocket connections terminated at stateless WebSocket Gateway nodes.
- **User-to-Server Mapping**: A distributed in-memory session registry (Redis Cluster) maps `userId -> gateway_server_id`.
- **Message Dispatch**: When Alice sends a message to Bob:
  1. Alice's gateway writes the message to the Message Store (Cassandra) with status `SENT`.
  2. Gateway queries Redis for Bob's active server.
  3. If Bob is online, Redis Pub/Sub routes the message to Bob's gateway instance, which pushes it over his open WebSocket.
  4. If Bob is offline, the gateway enqueues a Mobile Push Notification (FCM/APNs).
keyIdea: Use WebSockets for real-time delivery, Redis Pub/Sub for inter-gateway routing, and wide-column storage partitioned by chat room for sequential history reads.

concepts.title: Heartbeat Presence
concepts.body: Clients emit heartbeats every 30 seconds into Redis with a 60-second TTL. If a heartbeat expires without renewal, user state flips to Offline.

concepts.title: Message Delivery Receipts
concepts.body: Three-stage state machine: Sent (single check), Delivered (double gray checks), Read (double blue checks).

examples: Discord running thousands of Elixir/Erlang BEAM nodes for massive chat guild routing.

resources.title: How Discord Stores Billions of Messages

quiz.prompt: Why is Cassandra or ScyllaDB preferred over relational SQL databases for chat message history?
options: Cassandra delivers massive sequential write throughput and efficient range scans by message timestamp within a chat room partition
Cassandra runs natively in browser memory
SQL databases cannot store UTF-8 emojis
quiz.explanation: Cassandra's LSM-tree architecture allows high-throughput writes and fast sequential reads partitioned by `(channel_id, message_id)`.
